Definition: from a primary ὄλλυμι (to destroy; a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment:--destruction.
BiblicalUsage: Olethros is destruction, ruin, the end of what God judges. Paul delivers the offender to Satan for the destruction of the flesh in 1 Corinthians 5:5, that the spirit may be saved, and warns in 1 Thessalonians 5:3 that sudden destruction comes when men say peace and safety. The heaviest use is 2 Thessalonians 1:9: everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and 1 Timothy 6:9, where the love of riches drowns men in destruction and perdition.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe destruction in Scripture is never an accident, it is the end of a road chosen, and the same word that warns the greedy also hopes for the offender's spirit to be saved. My position is that everlasting destruction is real and terrible, and it is exactly why the gospel must be preached.
